Chapter 04100 BPMPROCESSING

SkyTrain

The city keeps time by the train.

Terminal City runs from the port to the park to the far side of the inlet, and all of it keeps the same time. Not by any clock. By the train. Doors, chimes, arrivals, crossings, the same intervals all day: a city-sized metronome that thousands of commuters happen to ride.

You will not see anything strange on the train. The evidence is in the timing. A train pulls in at the exact moment a song changes three districts away. A door chime lands on the beat in your headphones. Two things with no connection line up a little too perfectly, once, and then again.

The Old Line remembers routes the city forgot. The Freight carries things away. The SkyTrain does neither. It only keeps time, and because it does, the rest of the city can agree on when things happen. Every door opens at once.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
